guarantees.claim: encoded_key_block[0] is always assigned as the concatenation of encoded_key[0] and encode_bytepad.
When EnMasking is true, encoded_key_block[1] is assigned as the concatenation of encoded_key[1] and 16'h0.

assumptions.claim: encoded_key[0] and encoded_key[1] (when used) each have a bit-width equal to MaxEncodedKeyW.
assumptions.risk: Width mismatch leads to truncated or padded concatenation, corrupting the key block.

assumptions.claim: If EnMasking is true, the design must ensure that encoded_key array has a valid element at index 1, i.e., Share >= 2.
assumptions.risk: Array index out-of-bounds, causing elaboration error or undriven signal.
If narrower, zero-extended; if wider, upper bits truncated, altering the bytepad value.

uncertain_points.claim: In masked mode (EnMasking), share 0 receives encode_bytepad, but share 1 is forced to 16'h0. If encode_bytepad carries sensitive information, this discrepancy may leave the bytepad unmasked.
uncertain_points.risk: Potential side-channel leakage of bytepad content through share 0's power/EM signature.

uncertain_points.claim: When EnMasking is false, encoded_key_block[1] is not driven. Downstream consumers may inadvertently use share 1, causing X propagation.
uncertain_points.risk: Functional failure or simulation X-optimism if share 1 is not properly gated.

uncertain_points.claim: If Share > 2, only encoded_key_block[0] and [1] are driven; all higher indices (2..Share-1) remain undriven.
uncertain_points.risk: Undriven shares may cause X propagation if the rest of the design expects them.
